## What This Is

**If you run Claude Code in auto mode, apply this update.** Through v3.19.1 the Outward Gate asked before every CLI deploy, once per service per session. In auto mode that meant a click on each deploy you had already asked for, in every session that deployed, and a session running in parallel sat stopped until you came back to it.

Deploys now pass quietly. Secret writes still ask. A connected server you launched read-only passes whole.

## The Defects

**An ask with nothing to decide.** v3.19.0 added CLI deploys to the gate beside secret writes, and both asked. A deploy is the act you directed. Asking again before it adds a click and no protection, and the click lands on whoever is running the session.

**A read-only server treated as a writer.** The gate decides an MCP tool by its leading verb. A database server launched with `--read-only` refuses every write, yet its `execute_sql` has no read verb, so it asked.

## The Fix

**Deploys are quiet.** `fly deploy`, `wrangler deploy`, `wrangler publish`, `wrangler versions deploy`, `vercel deploy`, `vercel --prod`, `vercel promote` and `npm run deploy` are logged as `quiet` in `.runtime/outward-gate.log`. They are never asked and never recorded as consent.

**Secret writes still ask**, once per service per session. On fly: `secrets set`, `unset` and `import`. On wrangler: `secret put`, `delete` and `bulk`. On vercel: `env add`, `rm`, `remove` and `update`.

**The asking act wins.** When one command holds a quiet act and an asking act, such as `wrangler deploy && wrangler secret put KEY`, it asks. A quiet deploy records no consent, so it never opens the door to a secret write on the same service later in the session.

**A `--read-only` server passes whole.** The gate reads `.mcp.json` on every call. A server whose `args` include `--read-only` passes. Remove the flag and the next write asks again, with no edit to the gate. An unreadable `.mcp.json` yields no read-only servers, so the gate fails toward asking.

**Unchanged:** MCP writes on other servers ask, `openServers` still passes a server whole, and the scripts and commands you name in `outward-gate.config.json` still ask.

**The test.** `hooks-selftest.mjs` now proves each rule. Four deploys are quiet and each leaves its `quiet` log line, which a gate that did nothing would not write. A chained deploy and secret write asks. A quiet deploy that ran leaves no consent behind. A `--read-only` server passes and asks again once the flag is gone. An unreadable `.mcp.json` asks.

## If You Are Updating an Existing Vault

1. **Apply the gate files:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/se-update.mjs" --check` then `--apply` for `outward-gate.mjs` and `hooks-selftest.mjs` under `Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/`. No settings change: the gate is already registered.
2. **If you want your own deploy command asked**, name it in `outwardCommands` in `outward-gate.config.json`. Commands you name there still ask.
3. **Fire the positive control:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/hooks-selftest.mjs"`, then the same with `--negative-control`. Expect zero failures and `vacuous=0`.
4. **If your agent has customized the gate**, hand it this spec rather than the diff: built-in CLI deploys are quiet (logged, never asked, never consent); secret writes ask once per service per session; an asking act in the same command outranks a quiet one; an MCP server launched with `--read-only` in `.mcp.json` passes whole, read on every call. The tests in `hooks-selftest.mjs` are the acceptance suite. The recipient owns the code. This file owns the standard.

## Prerequisites

v3.19.1. Node on PATH, as the README requires.

## Optional?

No. A gate that asks where there is nothing to decide teaches you to click yes, and that habit is what a real ask has to get past.
